headline: Supreme Court Directs Historical Figures To File Formal Defamation Complaints From The Afterlife
body:
In a landmark judgment that significantly expands the reach of the Indian judicial system, the Supreme Court has ruled that deceased historical figures seeking justice for alleged defamation must now physically appear in court to file their complaints. The bench clarified that mere mention of historical events or controversial past figures in political speeches cannot be prosecuted unless the aggrieved party can provide a notarized power of attorney from the great beyond.

“The court is tired of acting as a proxy for spirits who feel their legacy is being misunderstood by the current electorate,” said a senior judicial registrar who asked to remain anonymous. “If a freedom fighter or a historical icon feels their reputation has been tarnished by a politician, they are welcome to haunt the courtroom, provided they bring a valid death certificate and a lawyer registered with the Bar Council of the Underworld.”

Legal experts note that this will effectively put an end to historical grievance politics, as most 19th-century figures are currently unavailable for cross-examination. The Ministry of Law and Justice has reportedly been instructed to install 'spirit-friendly' witness boxes in all district courts to accommodate the influx of spectral plaintiffs expected to file defamation suits before the next election cycle.

Political analysts believe the ruling will leave many political parties scrambling to find new campaign strategies that do not involve arguing about people who have been buried for over eighty years. “It’s a massive relief for our litigation team,” said a spokesperson for a major national party. “We can finally move on to arguing about things that are actually happening today, like why the city's potholes have developed their own independent micro-climates.”
caption: The Supreme Court has made it official: If you want to sue for defamation, you must be alive and present. Historical figures will now have to manage their own PR from the beyond. #SupremeCourt #History #Politics #Law (satire)
